title: How many sixth pieces fill the length of one half?
description: On the fraction wall, sixth pieces are laid end to end along the row of halves. Six sixth pieces fill the whole, so half of them fill one half, and Keeko doubts it by reading the number two in one half as the count.
teaching_notes: One idea: six sixth pieces make one whole, so one half needs half of six pieces. Watch for students who read the denominator as the number of pieces that fill the length.

source: Using a fraction wall with rows of halves and sixths, how ma
video_script.why: The child counts how many pieces of one sixth fill one half by using the fact that six sixths make one whole.
video_script.substitution: none: the book's own fraction wall with rows of halves and sixths
video_script.anchor: the fraction wall of the book: one whole and rows of equal pieces
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says two pieces, because one half has a two in it. Two sixth pieces laid on the half piece leave a gap at the end; the two in one half tells how many halves fill the whole, not how many sixths.
video_script.payoff_line: Three pieces of one sixth make the length of one half
video_script.fraction_reading: one half, one sixth, three sixths, six sixths
maths_rules: fraction wall rows of halves and sixths
1/2 is half of the whole, so it needs half of 6 pieces
6 divided by 2 = 3, so 3 pieces of 1/6 make 1/2 (3/6 = 1/2)
slip: Keeko thinks 2 pieces because 1/2 has a 2 in it; 2 pieces of 1/6 are 2/6, which is less than 1/2
video_script.design: One idea: count the sixth pieces that make the whole, then take half. The sixth pieces are laid end to end under the row of halves.
